A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, Appendices A and B, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original reinforcement-learning experiments with 1.5B and 7B models, benchmark results, training curves, and component ablations in Section 5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations, training curves, and ablation results reported in Section 5 and Tables 1–3.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the temperature scheduler, and the annealing procedure remain unchanged. The added statement about temperature scaling during the training forward pass clarifies implementation; it does not establish a revised procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same MATH, AIME, Omni-MATH, and AMC training sources and evaluate on AIME 2024, AMC 2023, MATH 500, and OlympiadBench. Appendix B retains the same dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain GRPO and DAPO and the same temperature, entropy-regularization, annealing, and rollout-allocation comparison configurations. The newly cited Zeng et al. work is not evaluated as a comparator.

E3.justification: The data splits, model sizes, 480-step training budget, rollout counts, response-length limits, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Section 5.3 retains 128 samples for AIME/AMC and 16 for the larger benchmarks; no new evaluation protocol is introduced.

E4.justification: Sections 5.3–5.4 retain the same temperature-scheduling, entropy-regularization, annealing, and dynamic-rollout analyses. The annealing sensitivity discussion, training curves, and all-incorrect-rollout analysis are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three experimental repetitions and report averages across runs. The uncertainty descriptions and shaded variability bands are unchanged, with no added seed information or statistical tests.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–3 and the plotted content of all 11 figures match. For example, Table 1 retains the proposed 7B model's AIME 2024 pass@1/pass@16 scores of 42.81/76.66. No results or findings are added or removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, equations, and Appendix A derivation are unchanged, including the low-entropy and logit-gap approximations underlying temperature adjustment. No assumptions or mathematical arguments are added or corrected.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient rollout allocation, exploration through temperature scheduling, and benchmark improvements over GRPO. Their scientific scope and strength are unchanged.

C2.justification: The explanations of entropy regularization, annealing's exploration–precision tradeoff, and DAPO performance remain unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning rollout budgets, untested difficulty-dependent temperatures, and experiments restricted to GRPO and mathematics.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 newly states that logits are also divided by temperature during forward propagation after sampling, ensuring consistency between training and sampling distributions. This improves implementation documentation; the hardware, hyperparameters, data preparation, and code/data access statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds Zeng et al. (2024), B-star, and describes its related use of discrete temperature adjustments to maintain exploration during self-improvement. The corresponding reference is added without broader changes to research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds brief passages in Sections 2 and 4.2 and updates the affiliation and correspondence block. The remaining narrative, section order, and appendix structure are retained.

P2.justification: The figures and tables retain their content and designs. Layout changes include text reflow, removal of page-number footers, and relocation of Figure 11 from PDF page 12 to page 13.

improvement.justification: The added Section 4.2 detail reduces ambiguity about implementing temperature scaling consistently during training and sampling. The new related-work discussion also improves attribution and context. These are limited gains in reproducibility and positioning; the empirical evidence and theoretical arguments remain unchanged.
